name: tou_home_cool_bank_owner_leaves_1404
description: Issue #1404 review: the owner leaves at 15:40 during a home pre-cool; the Away bank takes over and the Away band is widened to 83 F for the 16:15-21:00 period, which every surface now quotes. Since Issue #1409 the change writes the Away bank once (cool 77 F at 15:40), not the setback then the bank.

assertions.reason: Leaving at 15:40 inside the bank window: the Away bank target (cool 77 F) is written once, at the change, with no Away setback (cool 80 F) first (Issue #1409: that pair could stop the AC and restart it five minutes later). The review's S3 row (commanded 77 F by 15:45, the pair unpinned) is tightened to this now that #1409 is fixed.
Nothing is written between the Away bank and the high-cost period's start.
At 16:15 only the Away period-start timer writes (the widened setback, cool 83 F): the home bank-end timer was cancelled by the occupancy change.
During the widened period the thresholds quote the widened band.
The briefing quotes the widened edge the thermostat is told (was 80 F).
The chart draws the widened band (was 60-80 F).

value.action: High-cost period ends — setback back to 80°F

assertions.reason: Next Automation names the end of the widening (was 'Pre-cool ceiling (70°F)' at 2:30 AM).

verdict.summary: Leaving mid-bank: the Away bank takes over, and the widened period is quoted everywhere
verdict.observed_behavior: Issue #1404 review: the owner leaves at 15:40 during a home pre-cool; the Away bank takes over and the Away band is widened to 83 F for the 16:15-21:00 period, which every surface now quotes.
verdict.expected_behavior: Occupant view: the thermostat and every surface follow the occupancy change mid-bank.
verdict.effectiveness: Fails on 6ebdb16: the briefing says Cool at 80, the chart 60-80, Next Automation 'Pre-cool ceiling', and the hold block is missing. Removing the chart/briefing widening fails those rows.
verdict.user_outcome: If this regressed, the person would read 80 F while the empty house is held to 83 F during the expensive period.
